page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n1 server family. It features 8 vCPUs and 30 GB of RAM, providing a memory allocation of 3.75 GB per core. The instance runs on an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon CPU operating at 2.3 GHz. This configuration consists of 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 45 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware features such as Advanced Vector Extensions, AES cryptography, BMI2, and FMA, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates that the n1-standard-8 delivers modest processing capabilities. In stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, performance falls within the bottom 25 percent tier. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are positioned in the bottom 10 percent and bottom 25 percent tiers respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large-block read and write operations, though small-block cached reads remain in the bottom 25 percent. Cryptography and database operations, such as Redis SET operations, also rank in the bottom 25 percent tier. For lightweight LLM inference using a 135M model, prompt processing is weak, but text generation speed achieves an average tier rating.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density suitable for legacy workloads or development environments that do not require high-performance compute. Given its dedicated CPU allocation but lower overall benchmark scores, it is best suited for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations rather than intensive real-time processing or high-throughput data pipelines.
